svg.data-vd-play-label: Play: one heartbeat, from the SA node to the ventricles (slowed)
svg.data-vd-steps: [[0, "The SA node, the heart\u2019s pacemaker in the wall of the right atrium, fires an impulse on its own: cardiac muscle is myogenic, so no nerve impulse is needed to start the beat."], [0.45, "A wave of excitation spreads through the walls of both atria, which contract together (atrial systole). On the ECG this is the P wave."], [1.6, "Non-conducting fibrous tissue stops the wave reaching the ventricles. It passes only through the AV node, which delays it about 0.1 s, so the atria finish emptying into the ventricles."], [2.7, "The impulse travels down the bundle of His in the septum to the apex of the heart."], [3.3, "Purkinje fibres spread the impulse up through both ventricle walls, so the ventricles contract from the apex upwards and push blood into the arteries (QRS complex)."], [5.0, "The ventricles recover (repolarise: the T wave) and relax. The SA node then fires again, starting the next beat. Nerves from the brain and adrenaline change how often it fires."]]
svg.title: Initiation of the heartbeat: the pacemaker and conducting system
svg.desc: Frontal section of the heart showing the SA node (pacemaker), the spread of excitation over the atria, the non-conducting fibrous ring, the AV node, the bundle of His and the Purkinje fibres, with an ECG trace drawn in time with the beat.
svg.text: How each heartbeat starts and spreads
Front view (the left side of the heart is on the right). One beat slowed about ten times. Not to scale.

g.data-info: Their thick walls contract once the impulse arrives through the Purkinje fibres (ventricular systole). The left ventricle wall is thickest.
Their walls contract as the wave of excitation from the SA node spreads through them (atrial systole), pushing blood into the ventricles.
Tissue between the atria and the ventricles that does not conduct impulses: the wave of excitation cannot spread straight into the ventricles, so the AV node can control the timing.
Branches that spread the impulse rapidly up through the walls of both ventricles from the apex, so the ventricles contract from the bottom upwards and squeeze blood up into the arteries.
Conducting fibres that carry the impulse from the AV node down the septum to the apex (bottom) of the heart, where they divide into right and left branches.
A small patch of specialised muscle in the wall of the right atrium, near the superior vena cava. Its cells depolarise on their own (myogenic), so it starts every heartbeat and sets the heart rate.
The only route for the impulse from the atria to the ventricles. It delays the impulse by about 0.1 s, so the atria finish contracting and the ventricles fill before they contract.
Records the electrical activity of the heart. P wave: the atria depolarise; QRS complex: the ventricles depolarise; T wave: the ventricles repolarise (recover).
g.text: time (slowed: about 0.8 s in a real beat)
Cardiac muscle is myogenic: the beat starts
in the heart itself. Nerves (from the medulla)
and adrenaline change only the rate.
2 Excitation spreads over the atria: atria contract
4 Bundle of His carries it to the apex
5 Purkinje fibres: ventricles contract from the apex up
6 Ventricles recover; SA node fires again
